gaps.sentence: You should stop ___ so much coffee late at night.
gaps.explanation: stop + -ing = end the activity: stop drinking coffee.

gaps.sentence: On the way to Rome we stopped ___ some photos.
gaps.hint: stop in order to do sth
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do; stop doing = finish doing. Here they paused to take photos.

gaps.sentence: She admitted ___ the last train and had to take a taxi.
gaps.explanation: 'Admit doing' — confess to a past action takes the gerund.

gaps.sentence: I remembered ___ the door, so I went back to check.
gaps.explanation: remember + -ing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather she ___ the accounts this month, to be honest.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather + subject' takes the past form for an unreal present preference.

gaps.sentence: He stopped ___ coffee before bed and now sleeps much better.
gaps.explanation: 'Stop doing' = quit the activity; 'stop to drink' would mean pause in order to drink.

gaps.sentence: He spent months ___ the application, only to be rejected in minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time doing something' takes the gerund.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford ___ another month abroad.
